As Indian media, where top journalists hungry for the limelight turned healthcare journalists in the post covid landscape, indulged in fearmongering around HMPV in China that has been around since 2000,

the lack of dedicated environmental journalism made sure that the Earthquake

nodes.author: Aiyub_Dawood
nodes.text:
in Tibet, Nepal & Bhutan, that killed 126 people didn't get the coverage it deserved, especially since rampant construction & power projects have made matters worse in the Himalayan seismic zone, which is a ticking time bomb, as seismologists have been warning since 2018.

Even

nodes.text:
the land subsidence in Joshimath, & parts of Himachal is something anyone is hardly talking about, while tourism is promoted, & more mining & construction projects are being celebrated as development.

Landslides across the Himalayan region from North to North Eastern India are

nodes.author: vishalsuchak
nodes.text:
@myasultan @Aiyub_Dawood 1. It's not just cow-belt politics. 

We're obsessed with cricket.
The amount of inane analysis & fanboying is insane. 

And then there's our celebrity fetish. 

News pushes stuff like

- Xyz celebrity spotted here/there
- Xyz celebrity bought a luxury house worth XXX crores

nodes.author: vishalsuchak
nodes.text:
@myasultan @Aiyub_Dawood 2. There have been lists of the money celebs make from endorsements.

And people take it as a good thing.

As if the celeb has done something great.

In other countries, they'd be seen as 'bikau'.

We do get upset with Akshay Kumar for the nationalistic films, don't we?

nodes.author: vishalsuchak
nodes.text:
@myasultan @Aiyub_Dawood 3. But no one thinks to call out the media and the people for lionizing celeb endorsements.

A recent article speaks of how Diljith Dosanjh started with 3K salary now has a private jet.

Emissions. They do more damage than we can handle. France is scrapping air-routes.

Hello?
